elements.scope_reason: Contains 'organophosphate poisoning likely' with its criteria (seven parts: pinpoint pupils; excessive drooling/sweating; excessive secretions; vomiting/diarrhoea; pulse < 60; BP < 90/60). The atropine dosing that follows is management and out of scope.

elements.problem: Six of seven parts are present with the right concepts, thresholds and units (SBP < 90 or DBP < 60 follows the gold-standard treatment of 'BP < 90/60'). Logic concern: the rule joins all criteria with a flat (or), so a poisoned patient with vomiting alone, diarrhoea alone, pulse 58 alone or DBP 58 alone is diagnosed probable organophosphate poisoning. The page lists these as a cluster (the cholinergic toxidrome) rather than as independent sufficient signs; the gold standard uses any2 for such clusters. 'or' is the loosest possible reading and over-fires on the non-specific members.

elements.problem: Flowchart node 'Toxic dose' leading to 'Refer urgently'. Whether a toxic dose was taken is determined by PIH/AfriTox and has no finding or measurement in the language.

Flowchart nodes 'Unknown poison or dose', 'Non-toxic dose and has symptoms', 'Non-toxic dose and no symptoms': routing to PIH discussion or advice, dependent on a non-representable toxic-dose determination.

rule_level_problems.problem: Flat (or) over the toxidrome criteria: any poisoned patient with vomiting, diarrhoea, pulse < 60, SBP < 90 or DBP < 60 alone becomes probable organophosphate poisoning. Vomiting and hypotension are common to many poisonings (e.g. paracetamol, iron, alcohol). The page lists the findings as a cluster; any2 (the gold-standard pattern for clusters) or a required specific sign (pinpoint pupils / drooling / sweating / secretions) would be a more faithful reading.

Does not reference (active_condition (snomed_concept "Organophosphate poisoning" "disorder")) as the briefing asks when the red box names a likely diagnosis. A patient meeting the organophosphate rule via vomiting/diarrhoea (not persistent) plus BP 85/55 and pulse 70 is probable organophosphate poisoning but not Urgent, although the page says manage and refer urgently.
No probable Shock rule for footnote 1's criteria; 'respiratory rate > 30' is encoded nowhere on the page and pulse exactly 100 falls between the footnote's '>= 100' and the red box's '> 100'.

No possible opioid overdose rule even though the page names 'opioid overdose suspected' with shallow breathing / respiratory rate < 12 and SNOMED has 'Overdose of opiate' and 'Morphinan opioid overdose'.
'Excessive secretions' from the page is absent and no substitute or SNOMED-gap note is visible in the rule file (checker cannot see the remaining-questions file).

'Feeling agitated' is an emotional-state concept; 'Psychomotor agitation' / 'Restlessness and agitation' match the page's clinical sense better and are not is-a related to it in either direction, so records of those would not fire the rule.

summary: The red box is encoded faithfully: all 13 criteria are present in both the check_for task and the Urgent priority rule with correct concepts, thresholds and units, and every check_for item is consumed. The main problem is the probable organophosphate rule, whose flat (or) lets non-specific findings (vomiting, diarrhoea, pulse < 60, BP < 90/60) alone diagnose organophosphate poisoning in any poisoned patient, and which omits 'excessive secretions'. Secondary gaps: the priority rule does not reference the organophosphate diagnosis, footnote 1's 'shock likely' criteria (including respiratory rate > 30) are not encoded, and there is no possible opioid overdose rule.
